messages:
mikeg: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak from last week I'm seeing a CPU-side regression in our nightly perf runs. GPU nsys timelines look normal, but host-side sampling shows a big increase in time spent in the Python scheduler and tokenization path. :thinking_face:

sara-ml: Can you paste the perf record command/output (perf.data) and any flamegraphs? We should check folded stacks to see which Python frames are hot.

mikeg: Repro steps + what I ran:
```bash
# reproduce microbench (inside venv)
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .
# small workload (50 batches of variable lengths)
PYTHONPATH=. ./bin/run_infer --model rdx-small --batch-size 8 --seq-len-dist zipf --batches 50
# perf run on host sampling user stacks
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- python ./bin/run_infer --model rdx-small --batch-size 8 --batches 50
sudo perf script > out.perf && ./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl out.perf > folded.txt
./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl folded.txt > perf-flame.svg
```
Summary from perf-script (top stacks):
- 36% python3 _scheduler.py:BatchScheduler.compute_schedule
- 22% python3 tokenizer.py:tokenize_batch
- 8% posix syscalls / context switches
- rest in C-extension copy/serialize steps

perf-bot: Automated nightly run #2024-03-14: created artifact at s3://redwood-perf/host/1765432100/perf-flame.svg (quick summary: host cpu time +28% vs baseline). :robot_face:

josh: Did we change the batching heuristics or the queue draining logic in the kernel-selector PR? I recall it changed how we break up long sequences into microbatches which could increase Python-level loop overhead. Link: PR #345 (kernel-picker) modified batching thresholds.

anya: Noted something similar on local runs — when KV-cache misses are high (cold prefix) we end up calling tokenize for many short chunks instead of a single vectorized tokenize call. That amplifies Python overhead. Quick log snippet showing many tiny prefixes and cache-miss on warmup:
```
[2026-03-16T10:22:41Z] INFO kvcache: miss for key prefix: user-msg-984 (len 12)
[2026-03-16T10:22:41Z] INFO batching: schedule microbatch sizes: [2,1,3,1,1,4]
```

sara-ml: Sounds like two possible contributors: (1) kernel-selector changed batching shape leading to more Python scheduling work; (2) KV-cache warmup causing extra tokenization calls. Two quick experiments: run with KV-cache forced-hit (pre-warm) and run with old batching heuristics (checkout pre-PR commit) to isolate. Also try `py-spy record -o pyspy.svg --native --substitutions` for a Python-native flame to confirm GIL-bound functions.

mikeg: I ran `py-spy` on a small repro. Folded result (top lines):
```
BatchScheduler.compute_schedule;tokenize_batch;_tokenize_one  42
tokenize_batch;_tokenize_one  18
cpp_serialize  12
other_frames  28
```
This suggests ~60% of host samples hit Python call stacks around scheduling/tokenize. Moving the simple scheduling loop into C++ would likely drop that dramatically.

josh: I'll instrument a tight microbenchmark to compare: old batching vs new kernel-selector batching. Can you paste exact git range? Also try `perf record -g -p <pid>` on a pinned CPU to avoid noise.

mikeg: Git range: commit a1b2c3d..HEAD (PR #345). Repro commands above. For perf with pinned cpu and minimal noise I did:
```bash
taskset -c 2 sudo perf record -F 200 -p $(pgrep -f run_infer) -g -- sleep 30
```
Then perf script -> folded -> flamegraph. The perf-flame.svg is at the s3 path from bot.

anya: :thumbsup: I'll run the two experiments (pre-PR baseline, and pre-warm KV-cache) and post the two svg links. If both point to low python scheduler time for baseline and high for new, we can either: (A) revert kernel-selector changes to batching shape, or (B) move scheduling hot path to C++/cython and ensure tokenization is vectorized.

sara-ml: Also run with `PYTHONMALLOC=malloc` and `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1` off/on? kidding but maybe try `-X tracemalloc=25` to ensure not extra allocations. We should also add a quick perf test to CI that fails if host CPU > 15% for this workload.

mikeg: Great. Will upload baseline+new perf artifacts and add a draft perf regression CI test. Thanks team — I'll post links when done.
